$comment: Records (protocols, experiments, literature library) and online literature search.
The record tools WRITE into the workspace, so their tasks are naturally
multi-step: add, list, update, then verify the update landed. The offline
grader runs the same chain in memory, so a change to the record format or to
the ids the tools allocate fails a test rather than silently changing what the
`literature-search` is the one ONLINE task: `molbio_pubmed_search` and
`molbio_pubmed_abstract` reach the live PubMed API, so what they return is
whatever PubMed answers today and there is no recorded value to pin. Its
assertions are therefore all `where: "answer"` and structural — a PMID
appears, a title appears — and `benchmark/verifications.mjs` deliberately
declares no offline invocation for it. See NETWORK_TASKS there.

tasks.instruction: Set up my lab notebook for a Gibson assembly. Save a protocol called "Gibson assembly" with the steps Mix, Incubate, Transform, then relabel its category to "molecular cloning". Finally log today's experiment — title "First assembly attempt", note that there were colonies on plate 2 — and read both libraries back to me so I can see what is stored.

assertions.note: the list command's rendering of the record. The `[category]` and `(3 steps)` suffixes were pinned in the first version and failed a run where the model had already RELABELLED the category to `molecular cloning` before listing — which is precisely what the instruction asks for.
the record id must be relayed: it is what every later update/remove call needs

tasks.instruction: Build me a small reading library. Add this paper: title "SPLICER: a highly efficient base editing toolbox", PMID 39609418, year 2024, tagged crispr. Then list the library and use the id it reports to attach a note saying I have read the methods. Export the library to BibTeX as lib.bib, then remove the paper using that same id and confirm the library is empty.

assertions.pattern: added 1 paper\(s\); library now holds 1 paper\(s\)

assertions.note: the id the list command reports. It is NOT the bare PMID: the library qualifies it with the scheme (`pmid:`), and update/remove only accept that form — a model that guesses the bare PMID gets 'no paper with id', which is a real usability finding this task can surface.
the added paper survives the round trip (it appears again in the list output)

the outcome of the sequence, in prose. Measured behaviour: a model that exports `lib.bib` as a DELIVERABLE often ends with 'I've presented lib.bib as the deliverable' and omits the title — the artifact carries it. The three tool assertions above already prove the add → list → export → remove chain ran and that the paper round-tripped, so the answer check is deliberately loose.

tasks.instruction: Search the literature for recent work on CRISPR base editing and pull the abstracts for the papers you find. Give me the PMIDs, the titles, and a one-line summary of what each abstract reports.

assertions.note: at least one PMID. This task is ONLINE and its tool results are live PubMed data, so NOTHING about the individual papers is pinned — only that the model retrieved records and reported them with identifiers. See NETWORK_TASKS in benchmark/verifications.mjs.
